title: GetChildren()
summary: Returns an array of all direct children of an instance. Iterate with `for _, child in parent:GetChildren()`. Order is not guaranteed.

reference.returns: Array of direct children (one level only). Order unspecified — don't rely on it.

explanation.whyItExists: Systems constantly need to act on a container's contents: round up spawn points, tag every part, count occupants.
whenToUse: Looping a folder's contents (spawn points, waypoints)
Filtering children by class: `if child:IsA("BasePart") then`
whenNotToUse: When you need the whole subtree — GetDescendants
When you're looking for one known child — FindFirstChild
tips: Combine with IsA filters for typed sweeps
Snapshot semantics: the array is a copy — later additions don't appear in it
commonMistakes: Assuming array order matches Explorer order
Modifying parenting while iterating the returned array (fine technically — it's a snapshot — but logic bugs follow)

examples.title: Count and filter
examples.code:
local spawnFolder = workspace.SpawnPoints

local count = 0
for _, spawn in spawnFolder:GetChildren() do
    if spawn:IsA("BasePart") then
        count += 1
    end
end
print(`{count} valid spawn points`)
